newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China says MFN status will also benefit U.S.
newsitem.headline: China says MFN status will also benefit U.S.

text.p: China said on Wednesday that the extension of its most favoured nation (MFN) status by the United States would also benefit Washington.
U.S. President Bill Clinton announced on Monday his decision to renew China's MFN status for another year, but the move is expected to face fierce oppostiion from Congress.

"We welcome this decision. The MFN status is a mutually beneficial treatment. Any review of the MFN status to China has an impact on the development of the Sino-U.S. relations," Chinese vice premier Li Lanqing told a meeting of Asia and Pacific businessmen.
"We hope the American government and Congress will take into consideration the overall interest of the two countries to fully develop the bilateral relations," he said.
Social conservatives, organised labour and other opponents are preparing for a fight, pointing to China's policies on human and religious rights, trade and other issues.
